transcript.text: Alright everyone, before I can make a binding decision on the production capacity policy for the image-processing pipeline, we need to run through the normal capacity review. I want to hear from FinOps, SRE, security, and customer support about any operational requirements or concerns with the current draft. The draft has 12 baseline workers, scales out at 100 queued jobs, uses any available processing region, and puts all customers in a single FIFO queue. Given we need to be in production before the seasonal traffic increase, let's get moving on this review.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: While reconciling this month's cloud invoice for another service, I confirmed that the available compute reservation applies to this pipeline only with exactly 18 baseline workers and a monthly capacity ceiling of exactly 24000 USD. The draft's 12-worker plan has no reservation commitment, and I haven't yet updated the capacity proposal. We should factor this into the capacity policy before Riley makes a binding decision.

transcript.text: I need to share a finding from a separate load investigation I ran this morning. During the expected burst pattern, I measured an 11-minute worker startup time. The pipeline needs exactly 6 warm workers with scale-out triggered at exactly 40 queued jobs to keep processing latency within the operating target. I have not yet filed this result in the capacity review, so it hasn't been factored into the current draft.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise a security concern before this capacity policy is approved. During an unrelated access review of the image-processing deployment manifest, I confirmed that customer-uploaded image data processed by this pipeline must run in exactly eu-central-1 and must use the tenant-managed KMS key named tenant_kms. The current draft permits any available processing region and does not specify this KMS key requirement. I have not yet opened the security finding, so this constraint has not been reflected in the draft policy. This needs to be corrected before Riley makes a binding decision, since the regional and KMS requirements directly affect which workers and regions can be used for capacity.

commitments.detail: Update the capacity proposal to reflect 18 baseline workers and the 24000 USD monthly capacity ceiling to secure the compute reservation.
File the load investigation result in the capacity review and update the policy to specify 6 warm pool workers with scale-out at 40 queued jobs.
Open the security finding and update the policy to restrict processing to eu-central-1 and require the tenant_kms KMS key.
Add the Lumen Media customer requirement to the capacity proposal and update the queue policy to enable a dedicated priority queue for Lumen Media.
